# ruststream-sqlx

> `ruststream-sqlx` brings SQL databases into RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them, through `sqlx`: a transactional outbox over any RustStream broker, and task queues in Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables.

This site holds the entry pages. The crate is documented item by item on docs.rs, and the framework itself on the RustStream site.

## Site

- [Home](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/): the two components and where the rest of the documentation is

## Guides

- [The inbox broker](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-inbox-broker): task queues in the service's Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables, taken by row lock, by lease or by advisory lock; what each handler outcome does to a row, and where "now" comes from
- [Row locks, leases or advisory locks](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#row-locks-leases-or-advisory-locks): the three forms a queue table takes its rows in, what each holds while a handler runs, and when to declare `#[field(locked_until)]` or `advisory_lock`
- [The lease form](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-lease-form): the claim that commits, the lease as the ownership token, its extension every half lease, `LeaseLost`, and attempts counted at the claim
- [The advisory lock form](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-advisory-lock-form): `advisory_lock = ".."` and its key, the claim of candidates, the lock released at settlement, on an unsettled drop and at `shutdown` with its counts, a pool connection per delivery in work, and how Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite keep the locks
- [A lock of the service's own](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#a-lock-of-the-services-own): `custom(lock, unlock)` with `Lock` and `Unlock`, and a dialect of the service's own that implements `Advisory`
- [Isolation and mode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#isolation-and-mode): `isolation = ..` and SQLite's `mode = ..` in `#[inbox(..)]`, which database opens which level, and the compile error for one its dialect does not open
- [FIFO groups](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#fifo-groups): `#[field(group, fifo = true)]`, one row of a group in work, the head in claim order, how retries move it, and a group kept in order by an advisory lock key
- [Databases](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#databases): what Postgres, MySQL 8.0.1 and MariaDB 10.6, SQLite and an `AnyPool` each serve
- [A dialect of the service's own](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#a-dialect-of-the-services-own): the traits a dialect implements for each form and for subscriptions by name, a built-in dialect wrapped to write one statement, and a driver outside sqlx
- [Startup checks and rows that do not decode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#startup-checks-and-rows-that-do-not-decode): what stops a subscription when it opens, and the decode-failure policy that settles a row whose columns do not decode
- [Batches](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#batches): one claim as a batch, settled together in the row lock form and row by row in the lease and advisory lock forms
- [Routes and by-name subscriptions](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#routes-and-by-name-subscriptions): publishing into tables through repositories and routes, `#[subscriber("name")]`, and what each costs per message
- [Testing a service on the inbox](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#testing-a-service-on-the-inbox): `TestApp::start_live` against a real database or an in-memory SQLite, and the real clock
